boards.name: AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM (on ESP32-CAM-MB USB board)
boards.notes: The ESP32-CAM has no USB port; it plugs onto the ESP32-CAM-MB board (CH340 USB serial on GPIO1/3, IO0 and RST buttons). Drawn from the camera side with the MB's micro-USB at the bottom: that is the end with the flash LED and camera ribbon connector, and the micro-SD slot is at the top. This matches the usual RandomNerdTutorials pinout picture, no rotation needed. On the MB the header pins sit inside its sockets, so wires go to the pin stubs on the camera side or to a breakout between the two boards. Only four header GPIOs are free (13, 14, 15, 2): GPIO12 must be low at power-up (it sets the flash voltage) so nothing that can pull it high may go there, GPIO4 drives the flash LED, GPIO16 is the PSRAM chip select, GPIO0 is the boot strap and GPIO1/3 are the USB serial port. GPIO2, 13, 15 have 47k pull-ups for the SD card. The VCC pin is a 3.3 V output (5 V on boards built with the other 0R jumper). The camera and SD card are not used. The red LED (GPIO33, active low) is on the back. The page button is the MB's IO0 button; there is no button on the ESP32-CAM itself.

reserved.0: boot strap, IO0 button on the ESP32-CAM-MB, camera XCLK
reserved.12: strapping pin: must be low at power-up (flash voltage), anything pulling it high stops the board booting

sd.note: Uses GPIO14, 15 and 2 (1-bit mode), which are also the header's I²C and UART pins: with the card on, only GPIO13 is left for parts.

boards.name: ESP32 DevKit / NodeMCU ESP-32S, 30 pins
boards.notes: DOIT ESP32 DevKit V1 layout. Pins listed top to bottom with the USB port at the bottom.

boards.name: ESP32 DevKitC / NodeMCU-32S, 38 pins
boards.notes: Espressif ESP32-DevKitC V4 layout. Pins listed top to bottom with the USB port at the bottom.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47
boards.notes: Has a 1.47" 172x320 ST7789 LCD, RGB LED (WS2812) and microSD slot on board; ESP32-C6FH4 with 4 MB flash in the chip and no PSRAM. Drawn from the LCD side with USB at the bottom; Waveshare's pinout picture shows the back of the board with USB at the top, so it is turned over here. GPIO4 and GPIO5 on the header are the SD card's CS and MISO and are kept free; GPIO9 on the header is the BOOT button. The LCD and SD card share GPIO6/7. TXD (GPIO16) has a 499 ohm series resistor. The ESP32-C6 has only one spare hardware UART (UART1).

sd.note: The board's TF slot (SPI on GPIO4-7, sharing GPIO6/7 with the LCD; the two take turns). Its pins are kept free anyway.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-ETH / ESP32-P4-POE-ETH
boards.notes: Wired Ethernet (100M, PoE on the POE version), no Wi-Fi: it gets its address by DHCP and has no setup network. The VBUS pin is the board's 5 V rail and is live on PoE as well as USB. Drawn with USB at the bottom, so the network jack is at the top; that is upside down compared to Waveshare's pinout picture. There is no user LED, and the BOOT button doubles as an Ethernet pin, so there is no page button.

sd.note: The board's TF slot (4-bit SDIO on GPIO39-44, power switched by GPIO45). Its pins aren't on the headers, so it costs nothing.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-Module-DEV-KIT
boards.notes: Raspberry-Pi-sized board with an ESP32-P4-Module (ESP32-P4NRW32: 32 MB in-package PSRAM, 16 MB flash, plus an ESP32-C6 for Wi-Fi 6/BLE over ESP-Hosted SDIO) and 100M Ethernet (IP101, PoE module header). Flash and use the console through the Type-C port marked USB TO UART (CH343P bridge on UART0 GPIO37/38, auto-reset via DTR/RTS). The other Type-C port, marked USB, is the P4's USB 1.1 Serial/JTAG on GPIO24/25. The 40-pin header is one 2x20 Pi-style block on the board edge, not two side rows. Here left = outer row (board edge: 5V, 5V, GND, TXD...), right = inner row (3V3, SDA, SCL...), listed from the RJ45/USB-A end down to the button end. That is Waveshare's board photo orientation; the header pinout picture is drawn rotated 180 degrees. The Type-C ports are on the long side, near the bottom in this orientation. GPIO54 (header pin 32) is the C6's CHIP_PU/reset and GPIO6 (pin 16) is wired to C6 GPIO2 inside the module, so neither is free. GPIO0/1 carry a 32.768 kHz crystal inside the module. GPIO45 (pin 39) switches the microSD power (low = on), and GPIO53 (pin 34) enables the speaker amplifier. GPIO39-48 are powered by the P4's internal LDO VO4. GPIO32/33 have 2.2k pull-ups (the I3C SH1.0 connector). There is no user LED, only a power LED. The BOOT button is GPIO35, which is also Ethernet TXD1, so there is no page button.

sd.note: The board's TF slot (4-bit SDIO on GPIO39-44, power switched by GPIO45). Its pins aren't on the headers, so it costs nothing.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-ETH / ESP32-S3-POE-ETH
boards.notes: ESP32-S3R8 (8 MB octal PSRAM) with 16 MB flash, W5500 SPI Ethernet (PoE with the optional PoE module), camera connector (OV2640/OV5640), microSD slot and RGB LED. Pico-style 2x20 header, drawn from the Ethernet-jack side with USB at the bottom; Waveshare's pinout picture shows the other side with USB at the top. VBUS is the 5 V rail and is live on PoE as well as USB; VSYS is the same rail after a diode. PresenceCam doesn't use the camera: leave the camera connector empty, because its pins are handed out to sensors. GPIO33-37 go to the octal PSRAM and can't be used. GPIO21 is the RGB LED. The ACT and LINK LEDs are driven by the W5500.

sd.note: The board's TF slot (SPI on GPIO4-7, its own SPI controller, so it doesn't slow the Ethernet). Its pins are kept free anyway.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-1.47B
boards.notes: Has a 1.47" 172x320 LCD, RGB LED, microSD slot and battery charger on board. Waveshare doesn't publish the header order in text, so the diagram shows the free GPIOs as a schematic: wire by the GPIO numbers printed on the board. Check that your board has a 5V pin before wiring a 5 V part; otherwise power it from the USB 5 V.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-1.69
boards.notes: Has a 1.69" 240x280 LCD, RTC, IMU, buzzer and battery charger on board. The 12-pin header is listed top to bottom as in Waveshare's pinout. These pins are for the V2 board; the first version used GPIO33-36 for the buzzer and power, which clash with the PSRAM. On battery, press PWR to switch on; the firmware then holds the power on.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3
boards.notes: Native USB (USB Serial/JTAG on GPIO18/19), so D6/D7 (UART0, GPIO21/20) are free for a sensor; the ROM prints a boot message on D6 at power-up. The C3 has only one free UART (UART1), so a UART sensor must use uart 1. Drawn from the component side with the USB-C port at the bottom, which is upside down compared to Seeed's pinout picture (USB at the top there): D0 is at the bottom right and 5V at the bottom left. Pins are labelled D0-D10 on the board. There is no user LED (only the charge LED). GPIO2 (D0) and GPIO8 (D8) are strapping pins: harmless for normal boot, but GPIO8 must not be held low when entering the bootloader, so they are last in the list. Comes with an external U.FL antenna that must be fitted.

boards.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C6
boards.notes: Native USB (USB Serial/JTAG on GPIO12/13), so D6/D7 (UART0, GPIO16/17) are free for a sensor; the ROM prints a boot message on D6 at power-up. Only UART1 is free, so a UART sensor must use uart 1. Drawn from the component side with the USB-C port at the bottom, which is upside down compared to Seeed's pinout picture (USB at the top there): D0 is at the bottom right and 5V at the bottom left. Pins are labelled D0-D10 on the board. The antenna is chosen by an RF switch: GPIO3 low powers it and GPIO14 low selects the built-in ceramic antenna (high = U.FL connector), so the firmware drives both low at boot. The yellow user LED on GPIO15 is active low (3V3 - 1.5k - LED - GPIO15). D0-D2 (GPIO0-2) are LP GPIOs. None of the header pins is a strapping pin.

sensors.name: HC-SR04 ultrasonic distance
sensors.description: Measures distance by sound, 2-400 cm, in a narrow cone. Needs 5 V, and its ECHO pin answers at 5 V: put a 1 kΩ + 2 kΩ divider (or any 1:2 pair) between ECHO and the board, or the pin may be damaged. The HC-SR04+ / RCWL-1601 3.3 V versions need no divider.

options.label: Also count as presence when something is closer than (cm, 0 = off)

sensors.name: HC-SR501 PIR motion sensor
sensors.description: Passive infrared: sees people moving, not people sitting still. Needs 5 V, but its OUT pin is 3.3 V. Set the jumper to H (retrigger), turn the time knob fully anticlockwise (shortest) and let the hold time setting do the rest. It needs about a minute to settle after power-up.

sensors.name: HLK-LD2410 / LD2410B / LD2410C 24 GHz radar
sensors.description: Detects people moving and sitting still, with distance. Same wiring for the LD2410, B and C; the pin order differs between them, so go by the labels printed on the module. Wire TX/RX for distance and signal strength, OUT for plain on/off; both is best.

sensors.name: VL53L0X laser distance (ToF)
sensors.description: Measures distance to whatever is in front of it, up to about 2 m. Shares the I²C wires with the OLED. Peel off the protective film.

options.label: Also count as presence when something is closer than (mm, 0 = off)

sensors.name: VL53L1X laser distance (ToF, long range)
sensors.description: Like the VL53L0X but reaches about 4 m. Shares the I²C wires with the OLED. It has the same I²C address as the VL53L0X, so fit one or the other. Peel off the protective film.

options.label: Also count as presence when something is closer than (mm, 0 = off)

displays.name: The board's built-in screen
displays.description: Uses the screen soldered on the board; no wiring.

displays.name: No display
displays.description: Readings are still on the web page and serial console.

displays.name: 0.96" OLED 128×64 (SSD1306, I²C)
displays.description: The common 4-pin blue/white/yellow OLED. Pin order differs between sellers: go by the labels.

layouts.name: Basic
layouts.description: One row per sensor reading with a bar for ranges, presence on top. Extra rows go to more pages; short-press BOOT to flip. Network and device pages follow.

layouts.name: Big numbers
layouts.description: One reading per page, as large as the screen allows; presence first. Short-press BOOT to flip pages.

layouts.name: Graph
layouts.description: Each reading with a graph of the last few minutes, and a presence timeline. One page per reading.

layouts.name: Tiles
layouts.description: A dashboard grid: every reading in its own tile, presence highlighted. Fits the most on one screen.

cameras.name: Arducam Mega 3MP / 5MP SPI camera
cameras.description: Takes a JPEG when a rule fires or from the web page. Any four free GPIOs work for CS, MOSI, MISO and SCK (the camera is the only device on this SPI bus). VCC takes 3.3 V or 5 V. The fixed-focus 3MP and the autofocus 5MP wire the same; go by the labels printed on the 6-pin header. Photos are kept in the chip's flash: 3 at 320x240 on 4 MB boards, 20 at 640x480 on 16 MB boards.

cameras.name: ESP32-CAM built-in OV2640
cameras.description: The OV2640 that comes on the AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM, on its fixed pins. Nothing to wire. Photos are 320x240 JPEGs, the newest 3 kept in flash (the 4 MB flash leaves little room next to the event log).

cameras.name: ESP32-P4 MIPI-CSI camera (OV5647 / SC2336 module)
cameras.description: A camera module on the board's MIPI-CSI ribbon connector (Waveshare OV5647 or SC2336 modules, 2-lane). The sensor is detected at boot; its control bus is the board's I2C on GPIO7/8, shared with any I2C display or sensor. Photos are scaled to at most 640 wide and stored as JPEG, the newest 20 kept in flash.
